notes: Dev ABox revision; edit property: functional (named_after is functional, asymmetric, inverse:eponym_of). The topic's chain is carried by d002, so this fourth edit covers the functional exclusion and the composition task on a history-of-mathematics fact. The subject's name does not contain the answer (Cartesian is from the Latin Cartesius). Related near: the functional exclusion (no inverse near question has a stored answer: 'which coordinate system is named after Newton' has none before the edit). Related far: the eponym's nationality, which Wikipedia states with the adjective in one sentence (stored). Derived: three compositions about Newton by name, one open (the city where the eponym died: Stockholm, then London) and two yes/no (gravitation; calculus, co-credited with Leibniz, so 'yes' is the credited answer). The binding through 'the rectangular coordinate system' was dropped after review: named_after is about a name, and the name 'rectangular' honours no one, so the question had no fair answer. For the same reason the Chinese prompt no longer uses 直角坐标系 (rectangular coordinate system); it asks about the English name 'Cartesian coordinates' (笛卡尔坐标系 would spell out the answer). Residual risk: Descartes's death in Stockholm is less famous than his nationality; the audit shows whether the models hold it. A birth-century question was dropped: Descartes was born in 1596 but is thought of as a 17th-century thinker, so the original answer is unreliable. Unrelated near keeps the relation (Euclidean geometry, Euclid); its reference differs from the new answer. infini-gram was unreachable (HTTP 403) when the queries were revised on 2026-11-11, so new evidence is Wikipedia quotes and Wikipedia search hit counts.
